record.paper_title: Multiparty Quantum Key Agreement: Architectures, State-of-the-art, and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can cluster-state or graph-state multiparty quantum key agreement protocols be characterized quantitatively enough to predict key rate, loss tolerance, and error thresholds as functions of the underlying graph topology and hardware-specific noise model, so that graph-structured entanglement can be used reliably for routing, error mitigation, and measurement-based key-agreement primitives?

evidence.quote: Cluster states, also known as graph states, represent a distinct class of multipartite entangled resources built by initializing qubits in the |+⟩ state and applying controlled-Z gates along the edges of a chosen graph.

This graph-embedded entanglement offers modular scalability (2D or 3D lattices) and potential robustness to certain loss and measurement imperfections, with topology-driven security and distribution properties.
Further work is needed to quantify performance metrics (key rate, loss tolerance, and error thresholds) as a function of graph topology and hardware-specific noise models.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple graph with |V| = n vertices, each vertex assigned to one of n parties. The associated graph (cluster) state is the n-qubit pure state

  |G⟩ = (∏_{(u,v)∈E} CZ_{u,v}) |+⟩^{⊗n},

where |+⟩ = (|0⟩+|1⟩)/√2 and CZ_{u,v} is the controlled-Z gate acting on qubits u and v. A multiparty quantum key agreement (MQKA) protocol based on |G⟩ is a procedure in which the n parties each hold one qubit of (possibly many copies of) |G⟩, perform local measurements (single-qubit Pauli or adaptive measurements as in measurement-based quantum computation), and through classical post-processing (sifting, parameter estimation, error correction, privacy amplification) produce an identical bit-string of length ℓ that is secret from any eavesdropper, including dishonest insiders.

Noise model. Fix a hardware noise model N consisting of: (i) an independent photon-loss / qubit-erasure rate η ∈ [0,1] per qubit; (ii) a depolarizing or Pauli error channel with rate p ∈ [0,1/2] applied per qubit before measurement; and (iii) measurement error rate q ∈ [0,1/2]. Let R(G, N) denote the asymptotic secret-key rate per copy of |G⟩ achievable by the optimal cluster-state MQKA protocol against general coherent attacks (composable security), let η*(G) denote the maximum loss rate η for which R(G, N) > 0 holds (with p = q = 0), and let p*(G) denote the maximum Pauli error rate p for which R(G, N) > 0 (with η = q = 0).

Problem. Provide closed-form or efficiently computable expressions, or matching upper and lower bounds, for the three functionals

  R(G, N),  η*(G),  p*(G),

as functions of the graph topology of G (e.g. degree sequence, girth, vertex connectivity, expansion, or local-Clifford equivalence class) and of the parameters (η, p, q) of the noise model N. In particular, determine whether for natural graph families (paths, stars, complete graphs, 2D and 3D lattices) one can rigorously establish:

(a) an explicit secret-key-rate formula R(G, N) achievable by an explicit protocol;
(b) loss-tolerance thresholds η*(G) and error thresholds p*(G) that scale favorably with n for at least one infinite family of graphs;
(c) a topological criterion on G that is necessary and sufficient for the resulting MQKA protocol to support measurement-based routing (i.e. distillation of an n-party GHZ-type secret-sharing primitive between any chosen subset of parties) under the noise model N.

artifact.status_search_result: No comprehensive characterization of cluster-state MQKA key rates, loss tolerances, and error thresholds as functions of graph topology and hardware-specific noise is available in the literature; existing work treats specific small graphs or specific noise channels and leaves the general quantitative characterization unresolved. The question is identified as a direction requiring further work and is not known to be solved.
